relevance_reason: The paper describes a mouse model with conditional Pkd2 deletion that shows craniofacial anomalies, and it reports facial features in ADPKD patients found by 3D facial analysis. This adds supporting evidence and other features for the PKD2 entry.

findings.statement: Khonsari et al. (2013) found Pkd2 expression in craniofacial tissues. They studied mice with conditional deletion of Pkd2 in neural crest-derived cells, made using Wnt1Cre. The mutant mice had many signs of mechanical trauma, including fractured molar roots, distorted incisors, alveolar bone loss and compressed temporomandibular joints, as well as abnormal skull shapes. None of these phenotypes was seen at embryonic stages, when the head is under no significant mechanical stress in utero. The authors suggested that Pkd2 likely plays a critical role as a mechanoreceptor in craniofacial growth.
quotes: we located expression in craniofacial tissues and analysed mice with conditional deletion of Pkd2 in neural crest-derived cells, using Wnt1Cre mice

Pkd2 mutants showed many signs of mechanical trauma such as fractured molar roots, distorted incisors, alveolar bone loss and compressed temporomandibular joints, in addition to abnormal skull shapes.

Significantly, mutants showed no indication of any of these phenotypes at embryonic stages when heads perceive no significant mechanical stress in utero. The results suggest that Pkd2 is likely to play a critical role in craniofacial growth as a mechanoreceptor.

findings.statement: Facial anomalies had not previously been identified in ADPKD patients. Khonsari et al. (2013) took three-dimensional photographs of ADPKD patients' faces and analysed them using dense surface modelling. The analysis showed specific facial characteristics in the patients, some of which correlated with those of the Pkd2 conditional mutant mice.
quotes: Since facial anomalies have never been identified in ADPKD patients, we carried out three-dimensional photography of patient faces and analysed these using dense surface modelling.
This analysis revealed specific characteristics of ADPKD patient faces, some of which correlated with those of the mutant mice.

relevance_reason: Case report of neonatal-onset PKD in a patient homozygous, through uniparental disomy, for an incompletely penetrant PKD2 missense variant. This bears directly on the PKD2 phenotype and its inheritance.

findings.statement: Losekoot et al. (2012) reported a patient with neonatal-onset polycystic kidney disease who was homozygous for an incompletely penetrant PKD2 missense variant. The homozygosity was caused by uniparental disomy.
quotes: This study reports for the first time a patient with neonatal onset of PKD homozygous for an incomplete penetrant PKD2 missense variant due to uniparental disomy.

findings.statement: Losekoot et al. (2012) noted that ADPKD caused by a heterozygous mutation in PKD1 or PKD2 usually begins in adulthood, and that renal cystic disease is generally milder in PKD2 patients than in PKD1 patients.
quotes: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), due to a heterozygous mutation in PKD1 or PKD2, is usually an adult onset disease. Renal cystic disease is generally milder in PKD2 patients than in PKD1 patients.

relevance_reason: Reports ADPKD patients with PKD2 mutations who also had left-right laterality defects, which extends the PKD2 phenotype.

findings.statement: Bataille et al. (2011) reported 3 unrelated patients with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) who also had left-right laterality defects: one had dextrocardia and 2 had situs inversus totalis. No left-right anomalies were found in other members of the 3 families.
quotes: PKD1 and PKD2 were screened for mutations or large genomic rearrangements in 3 unrelated patients with ADPKD presenting with laterality defects: dextrocardia in one and situs inversus totalis in 2 others.
No left-right anomalies were found in other members of the 3 families.

findings.statement: In 3 unrelated probands with ADPKD and laterality defects, Bataille et al. (2011) screened PKD1 and PKD2 and found a pathogenic PKD2 mutation in each: a large gene deletion, a single-exon duplication, and an in-frame duplication. In each family, the mutation was present in all tested relatives with ADPKD and absent in unaffected relatives. The authors suggested a possible association between PKD2 mutations and heterotaxy. They based this on laterality defects in Pkd2-null mouse and zebrafish models and on finding PKD2 mutations in all 3 probands, even though PKD2 mutations account for only 15% of ADPKD families.
quotes: A large gene deletion, a single-exon duplication, and an in-frame duplication respectively, were found in the 3 patients.
These polymorphisms were found in all tested relatives with ADPKD, but were absent in unaffected related individuals.
detection of a pathogenic PKD2 mutation in the 3 probands, although PKD2 mutations account for only 15% of ADPKD families.

relevance_reason: The title reports perinatal deaths in a family with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease and a PKD2 mutation. That bears directly on the PKD2 phenotype entry, but only the title is available.

findings.statement: Bergmann et al. (2008) reported perinatal deaths in a family with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease and a PKD2 mutation.
quotes: Perinatal deaths in a family with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease and a PKD2 mutation.

relevance_reason: Mouse Pkd2 knockout model showing laterality defects; animal model evidence for the PKD2 gene underlying ADPKD type 2.

findings.statement: Pennekamp et al. (2002) generated a knockout allele of Pkd2 in mouse. In addition to previously described malformations, homozygous mutant embryos showed right pulmonary isomerism and randomization of embryonic turning, heart looping, and abdominal situs.
quotes: We have generated a knockout allele of Pkd2 in mouse. In addition to malformations described previously, homozygous mutant embryos showed right pulmonary isomerism, randomization of embryonic turning, heart looping, and abdominal situs.

findings.statement: In homozygous Pkd2-null mouse embryos, Pennekamp et al. (2002) found that Leftb and nodal were not expressed in left lateral plate mesoderm, Ebaf was absent from floorplate, and Pitx2 was bilaterally expressed in posterior LPM but absent anteriorly. The embryonic midline was present with normal Foxa2 and shh expression, suggesting that polycystin-2 acts downstream or in parallel to shh and upstream of the nodal cascade.
quotes: Leftb and nodal were not expressed in the left lateral plate mesoderm (LPM), and Ebaf was absent from floorplate. Pitx2 was bilaterally expressed in posterior LPM but absent anteriorly.
The embryonic midline, however, was present, and normal levels of Foxa2 and shh were expressed, suggesting that polycystin-2 acts downstream or in parallel to shh and upstream of the nodal cascade.

findings.statement: Pennekamp et al. (2002) found that mouse Pkd2 was ubiquitously expressed at headfold and early somite stages, with higher levels in floorplate and notochord.
quotes: Pkd2 was ubiquitously expressed at headfold and early somite stages, with higher levels in floorplate and notochord.

relevance_reason: Review of reported PKD2 mutations in ADPKD type 2; summarizes mutation spectrum, milder phenotype, and the two-hit mechanism.

findings.statement: Deltas (2001) reviewed the mutations reported in the PKD2 gene. Mutations of all kinds were spread over the whole PKD2 sequence with no apparent significant clustering. Most families had their own private mutations, but a few recurrent mutations were reported in unrelated families.
quotes: Mutations of all kinds have been reported over the entire sequence of the PKD2 gene, with no apparent significant clustering and with some evidence of genotype/phenotype correlation.
Most families harbor their own private mutations but a few recurrent events have been reported in unrelated families.

findings.statement: Deltas (2001) noted that PKD1- and PKD2-related polycystic kidney disease have clinically indistinguishable courses. However, PKD2 mutation carriers had a milder course, with average onset 10 to 20 years later and a lower probability of reaching end-stage renal failure. The author also reported some evidence of genotype/phenotype correlation among PKD2 mutations.
quotes: The only difference is that patients with PKD2 mutations run a milder course compared to PKD1 carriers, with an average 10-20 years later age of onset and lower probability to reach end-stage-renal failure.

findings.statement: Deltas (2001) suggested that renal cysts most probably arise after a second somatic event. This event would inactivate the inherited normal allele of the same gene, or possibly one allele of the other gene (PKD1 or PKD2), producing a trans-heterozygous state. Polycystin-1 and polycystin-2 were hypothesized to interact with each other and to take part in a common signaling pathway.
quotes: Renal cysts most probably arise after a second somatic event, which inactivates the inherited healthy allele of the same gene, or perhaps one of the alleles of the other gene counterpart, generating a trans-heterozygous state.
The proteins polycystin-1 and -2 are trans-membranous glycoproteins hypothesized to participate in a common signaling pathway, interacting with each other and with other proteins

relevance_reason: Reports a PKD2 truncating mutation (2152delA; L736X) segregating in a large ADPKD family with bilineal PKD1/PKD2 disease and trans-heterozygotes with more severe renal disease.

findings.statement: Pei et al. (2001) studied a large ADPKD family (NFL10) previously excluded from linkage to both the PKD1 and PKD2 loci. Of 48 family members screened by ultrasonography and genotyped at both loci, 28 were affected with ADPKD, and haplotype inspection suggested bilineal disease from independently segregating PKD1 and PKD2 mutations.
quotes: we studied the genetic inheritance of a large family (NFL10) previously excluded from linkage to both the PKD1 locus and the PKD2 locus

Twenty-eight of 48 individuals assessed were affected with ADPKD. Inspection of the haplotypes of these individuals suggested the possibility of bilineal disease from independently segregating PKD1 and PKD2 mutations.

findings.statement: In the NFL10 ADPKD family, Pei et al. (2001) used SSCP analysis to identify a PKD2 mutation, 2152delA (L736X), in 12 affected pedigree members.
quotes: Using single-stranded conformational analysis, we screened for and found a PKD2 mutation (i.e., 2152delA; L736X) in 12 affected pedigree members.

findings.statement: Pei et al. (2001) found that when the PKD2 mutation carriers in family NFL10 were coded as unknown, linkage analysis with PKD1-locus markers gave significant lod scores (greater than 3.0), strongly supporting a PKD1 mutation in 15 other affected members who lacked the PKD2 mutation. This was the first documentation of bilineal disease in ADPKD, and the authors cautioned that bilineal disease must be considered as a confounder in the search for a PKD3 locus.
quotes: when the disease status of these individuals was coded as "unknown" in linkage analysis, we also found, with markers at the PKD1 locus, significant LOD scores (i.e., >3.0)
These findings strongly support the presence of a PKD1 mutation in 15 other affected pedigree members, who lack the PKD2 mutation.
The presence of bilineal disease as a confounder needs to be considered seriously in the search for the elusive PKD3 locus.

findings.statement: Pei et al. (2001) identified 2 affected individuals in family NFL10 who were trans-heterozygous for both the PKD1 and PKD2 mutations; they had more severe renal disease than individuals with either mutation alone. The authors concluded that trans-heterozygous PKD1/PKD2 mutations in humans are not necessarily embryonically lethal.
quotes: Two additional affected individuals had trans-heterozygous mutations involving both genes, and they had renal disease that was more severe than that in affected individuals who had either mutation alone.
In humans, trans-heterozygous mutations involving both PKD1 and PKD2 are not necessarily embryonically lethal.

relevance_reason: Somatic second-hit analysis in ADPKD2 (PKD2) cysts, supporting a two-hit mechanism and a possible trans-heterozygous effect of PKD1 mutations.

findings.statement: Watnick et al. (2000) found somatic mutations of PKD2 in 71% of renal cysts analyzed from patients with ADPKD2, which supported a two-hit mechanism of cyst formation. In a subset of cysts that lacked PKD2 mutations, they found clonal somatic mutations of PKD1. Because the PKD1 and PKD2 products form heteromeric complexes, the authors suggested that trans-heterozygous mutations (a germline PKD2 mutation plus a somatic PKD1 mutation) may cause cysts.
quotes: Here we find somatic mutations of PKD2 in 71% of ADPKD2 cysts analysed.
Clonal somatic mutations of PKD1 were identified in a subset of cysts that lacked PKD2 mutations.
The products of these genes associate to form heteromeric complexes.

relevance_reason: The paper describes somatic PKD2 mutations in cysts from an ADPKD1 kidney, which gives a trans-heterozygous model. It also mentions earlier two-hit evidence in ADPKD2 cysts. This is pathogenesis evidence that bears on PKD2 cystogenesis.

findings.statement: Koptides et al. (2000) studied DNA from individual cysts in the kidney of a patient with ADPKD1 who had a germline PKD1 mutation. They found somatic mutations in the PKD1 gene in some cysts and somatic mutations in the PKD2 gene in others. The cysts with a somatic PKD2 mutation were therefore trans-heterozygous, carrying mutations in both genes. The authors concluded that this was the first direct genetic evidence that polycystins 1 and 2 interact, perhaps as part of a larger complex.
quotes: In cystic DNA from a kidney of an ADPKD1 patient, we showed somatic mutations not only in the PKD1 gene of certain cysts, but also in the PKD2 gene of others, generating a trans -heterozygous state with mutations in both genes.
One mutation in PKD1 is of germinal nature and the mutation in the PKD2 gene is of somatic nature.
Here, we provide the first direct genetic evidence that polycystins 1 and 2 do interact, perhaps as part of a larger complex.

findings.statement: Koptides et al. (2000) referred to their own earlier study of a human ADPKD2 kidney, in which 9 of 23 cysts carried somatic mutations that inactivated the inherited normal PKD2 allele. They took this as support for a two-hit loss-of-function model of cyst formation in ADPKD2.
quotes: recently we showed that somatic mutations inactivating the inherited healthy allele were present in 9 of 23 cysts from a human ADPKD2 kidney, supporting a two-hit loss-of-function model for ADPKD2 cystogenesis.

relevance_reason: Mouse models of Pkd2 deficiency that reproduce the human ADPKD phenotype and support a two-hit mechanism of cyst formation.

findings.statement: Wu et al. (2000) produced two mutations in mouse Pkd2. One was an unstable allele (WS25) that can undergo somatic rearrangement by homologous recombination to form a null allele. The other was a true null allele (WS183). Pkd2 -/- mice died in utero between embryonic day 13.5 and birth. They had structural defects in cardiac septation and cysts in maturing nephrons and pancreatic ducts.
quotes: an unstable allele (WS25; hereafter denoted Pkd2WS25) that can undergo homologous-recombination-based somatic rearrangement to form a null allele; and a true null mutation (WS183; hereafter denoted Pkd2-)
Pkd2-/- mice die in utero between embryonic day (E) 13.5 and parturition. They have structural defects in cardiac septation and cyst formation in maturing nephrons and pancreatic ducts.

findings.statement: Wu et al. (2000) found that adult Pkd2 WS25/- mice developed kidney cysts, pancreatic ductal cysts, renal failure and early death. Median survival was 65 weeks, compared with 94 weeks in controls. The authors suggested that kidney, liver and pancreatic cysts form by a two-hit mechanism. Adult Pkd2 +/- mice had no cystic disease or renal failure, but their survival was between that of the other two groups. The authors took this as a first indication that Pkd2 haploinsufficiency harms long-term survival.
quotes: Pancreatic ductal cysts also occur in adult Pkd2WS25/- mice, suggesting that this clinical manifestation of ADPKD also occurs by a two-hit mechanism.
As in human ADPKD, formation of kidney cysts in adult Pkd2WS25/- mice is associated with renal failure and early death (median survival, 65 weeks versus 94 weeks for controls).

Adult Pkd2+/- mice have intermediate survival in the absence of cystic disease or renal failure, providing the first indication of a deleterious effect of haploinsufficiency at Pkd2on long-term survival.

findings.statement: Based on their mouse models, Wu et al. (2000) concluded that kidney and liver cyst formation associated with Pkd2 deficiency occurs by a two-hit mechanism, in which a second somatic event inactivates the remaining Pkd2 allele.
quotes: to provide evidence that kidney and liver cyst formation associated with Pkd2 deficiency occurs by a two-hit mechanism

relevance_reason: The paper shows second-hit somatic mutations in renal cysts from a patient with PKD2. This supports a two-hit, loss-of-function mechanism for cyst formation in ADPKD type 2.

findings.statement: Torra et al. (1999) studied 30 renal cysts from a patient with PKD2 whose germline mutation was a deletion covering most of the PKD2 gene. Loss of the wild-type allele (LOH) was found in 10% of cysts. SSCP screening of 6 exons found 8 different somatic mutations, all expected to produce truncated proteins. Overall, at least 37% of cysts had somatic mutations.
quotes: We have studied 30 renal cysts from a patient with PKD2 in which the germline mutation was shown to be a deletion that encompassed most of the disease gene.
Loss-of-heterozygosity (LOH) studies showed loss of the wild-type allele in 10% of cysts.

Screening of six exons of the gene by SSCP detected eight different somatic mutations, all of them expected to produce truncated proteins. Overall, >/=37% of the cysts studied presented somatic mutations.

variants.as_reported: deletion that encompassed most of the disease gene

findings.statement: Torra et al. (1999) found no LOH at the PKD1 gene or at locus D3S1478 in the cysts, which showed that the somatic changes were specific to PKD2. They suggested that second-hit inactivation of the normal PKD2 allele could be a crucial event in cyst formation in ADPKD type 2.
quotes: No LOH for the PKD1 gene or locus D3S1478 were observed in those cysts, which demonstrates that somatic alterations are specific.
We have identified second-hit mutations in human PKD2 cysts, which suggests that this mechanism could be a crucial event in the development of cystogenesis in human ADPKD-type 2.

relevance_reason: A multicentre cohort study that compares the clinical phenotype and survival of PKD2 with PKD1 and with controls.

findings.statement: Hateboer et al. (1999) compared clinical data from 291 individuals with PKD2 in 31 families with data from 333 individuals with PKD1 in 31 families and 398 geographically matched controls, in a European multicentre survey. The median age at death or onset of end-stage renal disease was 69.1 years in PKD2, compared with 53.0 years in PKD1 and 78.0 years in controls. The median age at presentation with kidney failure was 74.0 years in PKD2 and 54.3 years in PKD1.
quotes: Clinical data from 333 people with PKD1 (31 families) were compared with data from 291 people with PKD2 (31 families) and 398 geographically matched controls.
Median age at death or onset of end-stage renal disease was 53.0 years (95% CI 51.2-54.8) in individuals with PKD1, 69.1 years (66.9-71.3) in those with PKD2, and 78.0 years (73.8-82.2) in controls.
Age at presentation with kidney failure was later in PKD2 than in PKD1 (median age 74.0 [67.2-80.8] vs 54.3 [52.7-55.9] years).

findings.statement: Hateboer et al. (1999) found that PKD2 patients were less likely than PKD1 patients to have hypertension (odds ratio 0.25), a history of urinary tract infection (odds ratio 0.50), or hematuria (odds ratio 0.59). Women with PKD2 had a significantly longer median survival than men (71.0 vs 67.3 years), but no sex influence was apparent in PKD1. The authors concluded that although PKD2 is clinically milder than PKD1, it has a deleterious impact on overall life expectancy and cannot be regarded as a benign disorder.
quotes: PKD2 patients were less likely to have hypertension (odds ratio 0.25 [95% CI 0.15-0.42]), a history of urinary-tract infection (0.50 [0.31-0.83]), or haematuria (0.59 [0.35-0.98]).
Women with PKD2 had a significantly longer median survival than men (71.0 [67.4-74.8] vs 67.3 [64.9-69.7] years), but no sex influence was apparent in PKD1.
Although PKD2 is clinically milder than PKD1, it has a deleterious impact on overall life expectancy and cannot be regarded as a benign disorder.

relevance_reason: Reports somatic second-hit PKD2 mutations in renal cysts of an ADPKD2 patient, which supports a two-hit mechanism for PKD2 disease.

findings.statement: Koptides et al. (1999) examined 21 renal cysts from both kidneys of one patient with ADPKD2 and found several novel somatic mutations in the PKD2 gene of the cyst epithelial cells. Seven of the 21 cysts (33%) carried the same C insertion in the inherited wild-type allele. In 2 other cysts, a nonsense mutation and a splice-site AG deletion were found in a PKD2 allele that could not be identified as either the inherited wild-type or the mutant allele. The authors suggested that ADPKD2, although dominantly inherited, arises through a cellular recessive mechanism, which supports a two-hit model of cyst formation.
quotes: We show in this report, for the first time, multiple novel somatic mutations within the PKD2 gene of epithelial cells, in both kidneys of an ADPKD2 patient.
From a total of 21 cysts examined, seven (33%) had the same C insertion within the inherited wild-type allele.
We suggest that the autosomal dominant form of ADPKD2 occurs by a cellular recessive mechanism, supporting a two-hit model for cyst formation.

variants.as_reported: C insertion within the inherited wild-type allele

relevance_reason: Reports a range of PKD2 mutations found in Canadian ADPKD families, including families linked to PKD2 and families with late-onset ESRD.

findings.statement: Pei et al. (1998) screened 11 Canadian families with ADPKD for PKD2 mutations. Four families had previously documented linkage to PKD2. The other 7 were smaller families in which 1 or more affected members developed ESRD at age 70 or older. Using SSCP analysis of all 15 PKD2 exons in 1 affected member per family, they found mutations in 8 of 11 families (about 73%). The detection rate did not differ between the PKD2-linked families and the late-onset ESRD families.
quotes: In this study, 11 Canadian families with ADPKD were screened for PKD2 mutations. In four families, linkage to PKD2 was previously documented. In the remaining seven smaller families, one or more affected members had late-onset ESRD at age 70 or older.

A spectrum of mutations was found in approximately 73% (8 of 11) of the families screened, with no difference in the detection rate between the PKD2-linked families and the families with late-onset ESRD.

findings.statement: Pei et al. (1998) found insertion or deletion of an adenosine in a polyadenosine tract ((A)8 at nucleotides 2152-2159) in exon 11 of PKD2 in 3 unrelated families. They suggested that this mononucleotide repeat tract is prone to mutation through slipped-strand mispairing.
quotes: In three unrelated families, insertion or deletion of an adenosine in a polyadenosine tract (i.e., (A)8 at nt 2152-2159) was found on exon 11, suggesting that this mononucleotide repeat tract is prone to mutations from "slipped strand mispairing."

variants.as_reported: insertion or deletion of an adenosine in (A)8 tract at nt 2152-2159, exon 11

findings.statement: Pei et al. (1998) reported that all of the mutations lay between exons 1 and 11 and were predicted to produce a truncated polycystin-2 lacking the calcium-binding EF-hand domain and both cytoplasmic domains needed for interaction with polycystin-1 and with itself. They found no correlation between mutation location and disease severity, and suggested that most PKD2 mutations are inactivating.
quotes: All mutations, scattered between exons 1 and 11, are predicted to result in a truncated polycystin 2 that lacks both the calcium-binding EF-hand domain and the two cytoplasmic domains required for the interaction of polycystin 2 with polycystin 1 and with itself.
Furthermore, no correlation was found between the location of the mutations in the PKD2 coding sequence and disease severity.
suggest that most PKD2 mutations are inactivating

findings.statement: Pei et al. (1998) noted that about 85% of ADPKD cases are caused by PKD1 mutations and that most of the rest are caused by PKD2 mutations. PKD1-linked families reach ESRD earlier than PKD2-linked families (mean age 56 vs 70 years).
quotes: Linkage studies have shown that the majority (approximately 85%) of cases are due to mutations in PKD1 on chromosome 16p, while mutations in PKD2 on chromosome 4q account for most of the remaining cases.
PKD1-linked families having earlier onset of end-stage renal disease (ESRD) than PKD2-linked families (mean age at ESRD: 56 versus 70, respectively)

relevance_reason: A mouse model study showing that losing Pkd2 in somatic cells causes polycystic kidney and liver disease that the authors describe as indistinguishable from the human disease, and that supports a cellular recessive (two-hit) mechanism.

findings.statement: Wu et al. (1998) introduced a mutant exon 1 in tandem with the wild-type exon 1 at the mouse Pkd2 locus, creating an unstable allele that undergoes somatic inactivation by intragenic homologous recombination to produce a true null allele. Mice heterozygous and homozygous for this allele, as well as Pkd2 +/- mice, developed polycystic kidney and liver lesions that the authors described as indistinguishable from the human phenotype.
quotes: We have introduced a mutant exon 1 in tandem with the wild-type exon 1 at the mouse Pkd2 locus. This is an unstable allele that undergoes somatic inactivation by intragenic homologous recombination to produce a true null allele.
Mice heterozygous and homozygous for this mutation, as well as Pkd+/- mice, develop polycystic kidney and liver lesions that are indistinguishable from the human phenotype.

findings.statement: Wu et al. (1998) found that in all cases, renal cysts in Pkd2 mutant mice arose from renal tubular cells that had lost the ability to produce Pkd2 protein. They concluded that somatic loss of Pkd2 expression is both necessary and sufficient for renal cyst formation in ADPKD, suggesting that PKD2-related disease occurs by a cellular recessive mechanism.
quotes: In all cases, renal cysts arise from renal tubular cells that lose the capacity to produce Pkd2 protein.
Somatic loss of Pkd2 expression is both necessary and sufficient for renal cyst formation in ADPKD, suggesting that PKD2 occurs by a cellular recessive mechanism.

relevance_reason: Reports a mutation screen of PKD2 in chromosome 4-linked ADPKD families that found seven new truncating mutations, which directly characterises the PKD2 disorder.

findings.statement: Viribay et al. (1997) screened all 15 exons of the PKD2 gene in chromosome 4-linked ADPKD families using heteroduplex and SSCP analyses. They found 7 new mutations, a detection rate of about 90% in the population studied. Every mutation caused translation to stop early: 4 were nonsense changes and 3 were frameshifting deletions, one removing 4 T nucleotides and two each removing a single G nucleotide. All mutations were unique and were spread across the gene with no evidence of clustering.
quotes: Here we report a systematic mutation screening of all 15 exons of the PKD2 gene in chromosome 4-linked ADPKD families, using heteroduplex and SSCP analyses. We have identified and characterized seven novel mutations, with a detection rate of approximately 90% in the population studied.

All of the mutations result in the premature stop of translation: four nonsense changes and three deletions. The deletions are all frameshifting, of four T nucleotides in one case and one G nucleotide in the other two.
All mutations are unique and are distributed throughout the gene without evidence of clustering.

findings.statement: Viribay et al. (1997) compared the specific PKD2 mutations with the clinical profiles of the ADPKD2 families and found no clear correlation.
quotes: Comparison of specific mutations with the clinical profile in ADPKD2 families shows no clear correlation.

relevance_reason: The paper screens PKD2 for mutations in families with type 2 ADPKD and reports a spectrum of 20 mutations.

findings.statement: Veldhuisen et al. (1997) screened the PKD2 gene by single-strand conformation polymorphism analysis in 35 families with the second type of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease and identified 20 mutations. Most mutations seemed to be unique and occurred throughout the gene, with no evidence of clustering. Besides small deletions, insertions, and substitutions leading to premature translation stops, they found 1 amino acid substitution and 5 possible splice-site mutations.
quotes: We have systematically screened the gene for mutations by single-strand conformation-polymorphism analysis in 35 families with the second type of ADPKD and have identified 20 mutations.
So far, most mutations found seem to be unique and occur throughout the gene, without any evidence of clustering.
In addition to small deletions, insertions, and substitutions leading to premature translation stops, one amino acid substitution and five possible splice-site mutations have been found.

findings.statement: Veldhuisen et al. (1997) suggested that the first step toward cyst formation in PKD2 patients is the loss of one functional copy of polycystin-2.
quotes: These findings suggest that the first step toward cyst formation in PKD2 patients is the loss of one functional copy of polycystin-2.

relevance_reason: The paper reports the positional cloning of PKD2 and nonsense mutations that segregate with ADPKD type 2 in families. This directly establishes the molecular basis of the entry.

findings.statement: Mochizuki et al. (1996) identified a second gene for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, PKD2, by positional cloning. They found nonsense mutations in PKD2 that segregated with the disease in 3 PKD2-linked families.
quotes: A second gene for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease was identified by positional cloning.
Nonsense mutations in this gene (PKD2) segregated with the disease in three PKD2 families.

findings.statement: Mochizuki et al. (1996) reported that the predicted 968-amino acid PKD2 protein has 6 transmembrane spans with intracellular N and C termini. It shares amino acid similarity with PKD1, with the C. elegans homolog of PKD1, and with the family of voltage-activated calcium (and sodium) channels, and it contains a potential calcium-binding domain.
quotes: The predicted 968-amino acid sequence of the PKD2 gene product has six transmembrane spans with intracellular amino- and carboxyl-termini.

The PKD2 protein has amino acid similarity with PKD1, the Caenorhabditis elegans homolog of PKD1, and the family of voltage-activated calcium (and sodium) channels, and it contains a potential calcium-binding domain.

relevance_reason: Linkage study showing that some Icelandic ADPKD families are unlinked to the PKD1 region on 16p13.3, which is evidence for genetic heterogeneity and a non-PKD1 locus. A partial exclusion on chromosome 2q is also reported.

findings.statement: Fossdal et al. (1993) used the polymorphic markers 3'HVR (D16S85), 16AC2.5 (D16S291) and SM7 (D16S283), which flank the PKD1 region on chromosome 16p13.3, to study linkage in 7 Icelandic families with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease. In 4 families the disease locus was in the PKD1 region, and 3 families were unlinked to 16p13.3.
quotes: to establish linkage status in seven Icelandic families with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)
In four families, the disease locus is in the PKD1 region, and three families are "unlinked" to chromosome 16p13.3.

findings.statement: In one of the unlinked Icelandic ADPKD families, Fossdal et al. (1993) excluded the disease locus from part of the long arm of chromosome 2. They supported the theory that more than 2 loci are responsible for ADPKD. Their data also confirmed that the YNH24 locus (D2S44) maps to chromosome 2q13-q24.
quotes: In one of the "unlinked" families, the disease locus is excluded from a part of the long arm of chromosome 2, and we support a theory of more than 2 loci being responsible for ADPKD.
Our data confirm the location of the locus YNH24 (D2S44) to chromosome 2q13-q24.

relevance_reason: The paper maps the second ADPKD locus (PKD2, which the paper calls PKD4) to chromosome 4q13-q23 using the Sicilian kindred where genetic heterogeneity was first found.

findings.statement: Kimberling et al. (1993) typed over 100 microsatellite markers spread across all chromosomes in informative members of the large Sicilian kindred in which genetic heterogeneity of ADPKD was first discovered. Renal ultrasonography confirmed whether each family member was affected or unaffected. The study localized a second ADPKD gene to chromosome 4q13-q23, flanked by markers D4S231 and D4S414, a segment of about 9 cM. The authors designated the new locus PKD4.
quotes: Over 100 microsatellite markers, distributed across all chromosomes, have been typed on informative family members from the large Sicilian kindred in which the genetic heterogeneity was first discovered.
This search has resulted in the successful localization of a second ADPKD gene to chromosome 4q. It was found to be flanked by the markers D4S231 and D4S414, defining a segment that spans about 9 cM.
The new locus has been designated PKD4.

findings.statement: Kimberling et al. (1993) designated the second ADPKD locus, on chromosome 4q, as PKD4.
quotes: The new locus has been designated PKD4.

findings.statement: Kimberling et al. (1993) noted that at least two loci exist for ADPKD: one on 16p, and a second, less common locus that had not been mapped before this study. They stated that using flanking markers for both PKD1 and the new 4q locus would improve the accuracy of subtype diagnosis and of linkage-based presymptomatic diagnosis, by reducing errors caused by genetic heterogeneity.
quotes: At least two loci are known to exist for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD). One was localized to 16p, but the second less common locus has remained unlinked.
This will improve the accuracy of linkage-based presymptomatic diagnoses by reducing the error due to genetic heterogeneity.

relevance_reason: The paper reports linkage mapping of the second ADPKD gene (PKD2) to chromosome 4.

findings.statement: Peters et al. (1993) assigned a second gene for ADPKD to chromosome 4 using highly polymorphic microsatellite markers. In 8 families with clear evidence against linkage to chromosome 16 markers, linkage analysis with markers D4S231 and D4S423 gave a multipoint lod score of 22.42.
quotes: Using highly polymorphic microsatellite DNA markers, we have assigned a second gene for ADPKD to chromosome 4.
In eight families with clear evidence against linkage to chromosome 16 markers, linkage analysis with the markers D4S231 and D4S423, demonstrated a multipoint lod score of 22.42.

findings.statement: Peters et al. (1993) noted that ADPKD is genetically heterogeneous: a gene on the short arm of chromosome 16 accounts for roughly 86% of affected European families. They identified 8 families that showed clear evidence against linkage to chromosome 16 markers.
quotes: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) is a genetically heterogeneous disorder.
A gene defect located on the short arm of chromosome 16 is responsible for the disease in roughly 86% of affected European families.

relevance_reason: Reports a Sicilian ADPKD family unlinked to the PKD1 locus on 16p13.3, with a milder phenotype. This is evidence for a non-PKD1 (PKD2) form and for genetic heterogeneity.

findings.statement: Jeffery et al. (1993) reported a family of Sicilian origin with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease that was unlinked to chromosome 16 markers. LOD scores for the polymorphic markers 3-prime HVR and SM7, which flank the PKD1 locus, were -1.4 and -2.33, respectively, with theta max of 0.5 for each marker.
quotes: A family of Sicilian origin with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (APKD) has been shown to be unlinked to chromosome 16 markers.
LOD scores for the polymorphic markers 3'HVR and SM7 flanking the PKD 1 locus, were -1.4 and -2.33 respectively, and theta max was 0.5 for each marker.

findings.statement: Jeffery et al. (1993) stated that the clinical phenotype of the Sicilian family was consistent with that of other ADPKD families not linked to 16p13.3, all reported from outside the United Kingdom. Those families showed milder progression than families linked to 16p13.3.
quotes: The clinical phenotype of this family is consistent with that of the other non-linked families with APKD reported in the literature, all outside the United Kingdom, which have a milder progression than those linked to 16p13.3.

phenotypes.text: milder progression of polycystic kidney disease

findings.statement: Jeffery et al. (1993) suggested that ADPKD may be much more genetically heterogeneous in the population than currently thought. Their reasoning was that clinic populations represent the most severe forms of the disease and that the non-PKD1 phenotype is less aggressive.
quotes: Assuming that a clinic population represents the most severe forms of a disease and non PKD-1 is a less aggressive phenotype, the degree of genetic heterogeneity for APKD in the population may well be much greater than at present suggested.

relevance_reason: Linkage study confirming and refining the PKD2 locus on 4q in Spanish ADPKD families.

findings.statement: San Millán et al. (1995) confirmed linkage of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease to microsatellite markers on chromosome 4q in 8 Spanish families in which the disease was not linked to 16p13.3. A maximum lod score of 9.03 at a recombination fraction of 0.00 was obtained with marker D4S423. Multipoint linkage analysis and study of recombinant haplotypes placed the PKD2 locus between D4S1542 and D4S1563, defining a genetic interval of approximately 1 cM.
quotes: We present confirmation of linkage to microsatellite markers on chromosome 4q in eight Spanish families with ADPKD, in which the disease was not linked to 16p13.3.
By linkage analysis with marker D4S423, a maximum lod score of 9.03 at a recombination fraction of .00 was obtained.
Multipoint linkage analysis, as well as a study of recombinant haplotypes, placed the PKD2 locus between D4S1542 and D4S1563, thereby defining a genetic interval of approximately 1 cM.

findings.statement: San Millán et al. (1995) noted that ADPKD is genetically heterogeneous, with a gene defect at 16p13.3 responsible in approximately 86% of affected European families and a second locus at 4q13-q23 a candidate in the remaining families; their 8 Spanish families were unlinked to 16p13.3.
quotes: In approximately 86% of affected European families, a gene defect localized to 16p13.3 was responsible for ADPKD, while a second locus has been recently localized to 4q13-q23 as candidate for the disease in the remaining families.

relevance_reason: Linkage study of Spanish ADPKD families identifying PKD2-linked families and comparing their clinical course with PKD1 families.

findings.statement: Coto et al. (1995) studied 17 large Spanish families with ADPKD using ultrasonography and microsatellite markers closely linked to PKD1 on 16p13.3. Five of the 17 families showed negative linkage to 16p13.3, and in these families significant linkage to the PKD2 locus on 4q was obtained.
quotes: We studied 17 large families affected by adult dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD).
Five of the 17 families showed negative linkage for the 16p13.3 markers. In these families significant linkage to 4q was obtained.

findings.statement: Coto et al. (1995) concluded that ADPKD in the Spanish population is genetically heterogeneous, but that mutations at only 2 loci, PKD1 and PKD2, are responsible for the disease in most if not all families; 12 of 17 families were linked to 16p13.3 and 5 to 4q.
quotes: Analysis of large families with ADPKD in a Spanish population indicates that this is a genetically heterogeneous disorder, but mutations at only two loci are responsible for the development of the disease in most if not all the families.

findings.statement: Coto et al. (1995) found that renal cysts developed at an earlier age in PKD1 mutation carriers, and end-stage renal failure occurred at an older age in individuals with PKD2, indicating that ADPKD2 has a better prognosis than PKD1-linked disease.
quotes: Renal cysts developed at an earlier age in PKD1 mutation carriers, and end stage renal failure occurred at an older age in people affected with PKD2.
Clinicopathological differences between both forms of the disease occur, with subjects with ADPKD2 having a better prognosis than those with mutations at PKD1.

relevance_reason: This paper is the first to show a second ADPKD locus that is not linked to chromosome 16p (alpha-globin). That locus is the basis for PKD2.

findings.statement: Romeo et al. (1988) found no linkage between autosomal dominant adult-type polycystic kidney disease and the alpha-globin genes on chromosome 16p in an Italian family. They concluded that the disorder can be caused by mutations in a second gene.
quotes: In an Italian family, absence of linkage between the disease mutation and alpha-globin indicates that the condition can be caused by mutations in a second gene.

findings.statement: Romeo et al. (1988) reported that the clinical features of polycystic kidney disease in the unlinked Italian family could not be told apart from those in families linked to chromosome 16.
quotes: The clinical features of the disease in this Italian family are indistinguishable from those found in the "linked" families.

findings.statement: Romeo et al. (1988) pointed out that because there are two polycystic kidney disease genes, linkage must be shown separately in each family before DNA-probe predictive testing can be relied on.
quotes: The finding that there are two polycystic kidney disease genes means that linkage must be demonstrated independently in each family before predictive tests with DNA probes can be used reliably.

relevance_reason: First report of a family with ADPKD not linked to the alpha-globin/PKD1 region on 16p, establishing a second ADPKD locus (PKD2).

findings.statement: Kimberling et al. (1988) described a 5-generation kindred descended from Sicilian immigrants with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease that was not linked to the alpha-hemoglobin complex on chromosome 16p. In linkage studies of 163 family members, 71 of whom were affected or at risk, the recombination frequency between the alpha-globin complex and the PKD1 region exceeded 24%, and the authors concluded that there is a second gene for ADPKD.
quotes: We describe a five-generation kindred, descendants of Sicilian immigrants, in which the disease occurs but without linkage to the alpha-hemoglobin complex.

In this family the frequency of recombination between the alpha-hemoglobin complex and the region previously shown to contain the mutation causing polycystic kidney disease exceeded 24 percent, indicating a mutation at a different locus.
We conclude that there is a second gene for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.

findings.statement: Kimberling et al. (1988) found that the clinical findings in the unlinked Sicilian-descended ADPKD kindred, in which diagnoses were confirmed by ultrasound, were indistinguishable from those in other families with polycystic kidney disease.
quotes: Diagnoses were confirmed by ultrasound examination.
The clinical findings in this family were indistinguishable from those in other families with polycystic kidney disease.

findings.statement: Kimberling et al. (1988) cautioned that, because of this locus heterogeneity, prenatal and presymptomatic diagnosis of ADPKD by linkage needs to be approached with caution until a method is found to tell the two forms apart.
quotes: This apparent heterogeneity means that prenatal and presymptomatic diagnosis must be approached with caution until a method is found to distinguish between the two forms of the disease.

relevance_reason: Reports a large ADPKD family that does not link to the PKD1 locus. This is early evidence that the disease is genetically heterogeneous and that another locus, such as PKD2, exists.

findings.statement: Bachner et al. (1990) described a large 3-generation family with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease. Ultrasound screening of 60 family members found 20 individuals, aged 10 to 80 years, with one or several cysts in only one kidney and 7 individuals with cysts in both kidneys.
quotes: We describe a large three generation family with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (PKD).

Ultrasonographic screening of 60 family members revealed 20 individuals, whose age ranged from ten to eighty years, with one or several cysts in only one kidney and 7 individuals with cysts in both kidneys.

findings.statement: In the family reported by Bachner et al. (1990), transmission of unilateral renal cysts appeared to be autosomal dominant, although some generations were skipped. The authors concluded that the family had a form of autosomal dominant PKD with reduced penetrance.
quotes: Transmission of unilateral cysts seems to be autosomal dominant, although there are some generation gaps.
We conclude that this family presents a form of autosomal dominant PKD with reduced penetrance and no linkage to the PKD1 locus on the short arm of chromosome 16.

findings.statement: Bachner et al. (1990) found no linkage between the disease and several markers of the PKD1 locus on 16p. Depending on the penetrance model and on how individuals with unilateral cysts were classified, lod scores for the 3-prime HVR marker ranged from 1.31 to -21.47 at theta = 0. Smith's test of heterogeneity gave a conditional probability of non-linkage between 0.9 and 1.0. The authors also considered other explanations: two distinct hereditary diseases in the family, or a new mutation in one branch together with a high frequency of isolated renal cysts.
quotes: Linkage studies with several markers of the PKD1 locus on the short arm of chromosome 16 showed no linkage with the disease.
Results varied from Z = 1.31 to Z = -21.47 (theta = 0). Smith's test of heterogeneity gave a conditional probability of non-linkage between 0.9 and 1.0.

Other hypotheses, such as the existence of two distinct hereditary diseases in this large family, or neomutation in one branch of the family associated with a high frequency of isolated renal cysts, are also considered.

relevance_reason: Exclusion mapping of the ADPKD2 locus from chromosome 1 in a large family not linked to chromosome 16.

findings.statement: Kumar et al. (1990) genotyped members of a large ADPKD family not linked to chromosome 16 for 12 marker loci on both arms of chromosome 1. Multipoint analysis excluded the ADPKD2 locus from the region between D1S81 (pTHH33) and D1S67 (pHHH106) on the long arm and between Rh and PGM1 on the short arm. This excluded the disease locus from about 61% of chromosome 1, about 160 cM.
quotes: Members of a large ADPKD family, unlinked to chromosome 16, have been typed for 12 marker loci located on both arms of chromosome 1.

Multipoint analysis excluded ADPKD2 from the region between D1S81 (pTHH33) and D1S67 (pHHH106) on the long arm and between Rh and PGM1 on the short arm. This excludes the disease locus from about 61% of chromosome 1.

findings.statement: Kumar et al. (1990) noted that autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease shows genetic heterogeneity: some families show linkage to markers on chromosome 16p and others do not. They studied a large family not linked to chromosome 16.
quotes: recent studies have shown genetic heterogeneity, with some, but not all, families showing linkage with markers on chromosome 16p

relevance_reason: Linkage study weighing the evidence for a second ADPKD locus (PKD2) that is not linked to PKD1; it concludes that the evidence is not compelling.

findings.statement: Elles et al. (1990) typed 24 families with adult-onset polycystic kidney disease for markers flanking the PKD1 locus on chromosome 16. The combined results gave a significant lod score in favor of linkage to PKD1.
quotes: Twenty-four families with adult onset polycystic kidney disease were typed for markers flanking the PKD1 locus on chromosome 16. The aggregated results gave a significant lod score in favour of linkage to PKD1.

findings.statement: Elles et al. (1990) found unusual features in 2 of 24 families: recombinations with markers flanking PKD1, including double recombinations, and, in one family, an unexpectedly high proportion of affected people. They considered whether the disease in these families might result from a mutation at a second locus, PKD2, not linked to PKD1. Using a test that compares the numbers of apparently nonrecombinant and doubly recombinant meioses, they concluded that neither their 2 families nor the published data on other families provided compelling evidence for a second locus.
quotes: Within this group of families two showed unusual features: recombinations, including double recombinations, and, in one family, an unexpectedly high proportion of affected people.
We consider the evidence that in these families the disease might result from a mutation at a different locus, PKD2, not linked to PKD1.
neither our two families nor the data published so far on other families provide compelling evidence for the existence of a second locus for adult polycystic kidney disease.

findings.statement: Elles et al. (1990) suggested that, for genetic counseling in families too small to give their own evidence for or against linkage, the extra uncertainty could be handled by using a higher recombination rate.
quotes: For genetic counselling in families too small to give internal evidence for or against linkage, the extra uncertainty can be handled by using a higher recombination rate.

relevance_reason: The title proposes a possible chromosome 2 locus for polycystic kidney disease, which bears on mapping and heterogeneity of a non-PKD1 form. Only the title was available.

findings.statement: Nørby and Schwartz (1990) proposed a possible locus for polycystic kidney disease on chromosome 2.
quotes: Possible locus for polycystic kidney disease on chromosome 2.

relevance_reason: Exclusion mapping of a second PKD locus in a large Sicilian kindred unlinked to chromosome 16; provides evidence for locus heterogeneity and exclusion data relevant to PKD2.

findings.statement: Kumar et al. (1991) studied a large Sicilian autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease kindred with over 250 members that was unlinked to the PKD1 locus on chromosome 16, supporting the existence of at least a second ADPKD locus.
quotes: Polycystic kidney disease (PKD) is a common autosomal dominant genetic disorder caused by mutation in at least two different gene loci.
A large PKD kindred, unlinked to chromosome 16, with over 250 members was studied using both DNA and classical markers.

findings.statement: In the large Sicilian ADPKD kindred unlinked to chromosome 16, Kumar et al. (1991) analyzed 29 informative marker loci on 11 autosomes; linkage with the disease locus was significantly excluded for 17 marker loci, and there was no evidence of close linkage with the remaining loci.
quotes: In total, 29 informative marker loci on 11 autosomes have been analyzed for linkage with PKD.
The data significantly exclude the linkage with disease locus from 17 marker loci and show no evidence of close linkage with the other loci.

relevance_reason: Abstract compares ADPKD families in Newfoundland that are linked and not linked to PKD1. In the 2 unlinked (non-PKD1) families, kidney cysts appeared later and ESRD started later, which separates the clinical course of the non-PKD1 (PKD2-type) disease.

findings.statement: Bear et al. (1992) studied 17 Newfoundland families with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease. In 10 families, ADPKD showed genetic linkage to markers for the PKD1 locus. In 2 families, ADPKD was not co-inherited with PKD1 markers.
quotes: In 10 families showing genetic linkage between ADPKD and markers for the PKD1 locus
In 2 families in which ADPKD is not co-inherited with PKD1 markers

findings.statement: Bear et al. (1992) found that in families whose ADPKD was not co-inherited with PKD1 markers, the mean age at onset of end-stage renal disease was 68.7 years (SE 1.7). In PKD1 families it was 56.3 years (SE 1.8; P = 0.01). In the 2 non-PKD1 families, only 11% of members younger than 30 years had kidney cysts.
quotes: The mean (SE) age of onset of ESRD is 56.3 (1.8) years for persons with the PKD1 form of ADPKD, and 68.7 (1.7) years for affected members of families in which ADPKD is not co-inherited with PKD1 markers (P = 0.01).
In 2 families in which ADPKD is not co-inherited with PKD1 markers, only 11% of members aged less than 30 years had kidney cysts.

findings.statement: Bear et al. (1992) estimated that in PKD1-linked families, ultrasonography gave false-negative diagnoses in 36% of members younger than 10 years and in 8% or less of older members. False-negative ultrasonographic diagnosis of PKD1 disease was unlikely after age 30 years. The risk of a false-negative result appeared largely restricted to families in which ESRD occurred relatively late.
quotes: rates of false negative ultrasonographic diagnosis are estimated as 36% below the age of 10 years and 8% or less thereafter
At ages above 30 years, false negative ultrasonographic diagnosis of PKD1 disease is unlikely.
risk of false negative ultrasonographic diagnosis appears largely restricted to families in which ESRD occurs relatively late

relevance_reason: Clinical comparison of non-PKD1-linked ADPKD (which corresponds to PKD2) with PKD1-linked disease, showing a milder phenotype; this is evidence for genetic heterogeneity.

findings.statement: Ravine et al. (1992) compared 5 families (49 affected individuals) with ADPKD in which the PKD1 locus had been excluded against 18 PKD1-linked families (285 affected members). Compared with PKD1 patients, non-PKD1 patients lived longer (median survival 71.5 vs 56.0 years) and had a lower risk of progressing to renal failure (odds ratio 0.35). They were also less likely to have hypertension (adjusted odds ratio 0.29), were diagnosed at an older age (median 69.1 vs 44.8 years), and had fewer renal cysts at diagnosis.
quotes: We identified 18 families (285 affected members) with mutations at PKD1 and 5 families (49 affected individuals) in which involvement of this locus could be dismissed.
Non-PKD1 patients lived longer than PKD1 patients (median survival 71.5 vs 56.0 years), had a lower risk of progressing to renal failure (odds ratio 0.35, 95% CI 0.13-0.92)
were diagnosed at an older age (median 69.1 vs 44.8 years), and had fewer renal cysts at the time of diagnosis

findings.statement: Ravine et al. (1992) concluded that ADPKD not linked to PKD1 on chromosome 16 has a much milder phenotype than PKD1-linked disease. No non-PKD1 family was ascertained through renal impairment clinics. Partly because of this milder severity, the authors suggested that the reported prevalence of the non-PKD1 genotype is probably an underestimate.
quotes: Non-PKD1 ADPKD has a much milder phenotype than that linked to PKD1.
Although most of the PKD1 families were ascertained through clinics treating patients with renal impairment, no non-PKD1 family was identified through this source.
Partly as a result of this difference in severity, the reported prevalence of this genotype is probably an underestimate.
